overall: The AG found the Cape Light Compact Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the four allegations arising from the September 16 meeting, and closed the matter with no orders.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board interfered with his audio recording of the September 16 meeting by moving his device to a different table location.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board's restriction requiring the recording device to be placed at the end of the meeting table near the teleconference speaker was a reasonable restriction because the recording device was able to pick up the sound from the Board's discussions from that location.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board refused to give him a printed copy of meeting exhibits that staff had distributed to members during the September 16 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, therefore, the Board was not required to provide Mr. Bibler with the records he requested during the meeting, and therefore the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by declining to do so.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair improperly cut off his questions to the Board during the public comment portion of the September 16 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Chair may decide who can address Board, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by refusing to entertain Mr. Bibler's questions.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board was hostile toward him when he tried to address it on September 16.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not mandate that public bodies adopt a particular tone when conducting business.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
